name: Limits_2b
questiontext:
A \({\bf rational}\mbox{ } {\bf function}\) is a quotient of two polynomials. Evaluate the following limit of a rational function: \[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}}{\left(\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}\right)}. \] If the limit does not exist, enter the value 1111 as your answer.

The limit is: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
The limit of the function \[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}}{\left(\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}\right)}. \]
is the same as the limit found by keeping only the highest power terms in the numerator and the denominator. Hence resulting in a limit of {{CT:4}}.

The limit of the function can be found by dividing the numerator and denominator by {{CT:5}}.

The function can thus be expressed as \[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}}{\left(\frac{{CT:6}}{{CT:7}}\right)}. \]

As {{CT:8}} tends to {{CT:9}}, all terms apart from the constant tend to zero.

Hence the limit is {{CT:4}}.
